newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KBB sees 1996/97 net down 58 percent.
newsitem.headline: KBB sees 1996/97 net down 58 percent.

text.p: Retailer NV Koninklijke Bijenkorf Beheer KBB said on Thursday it expects a net profit of about 61 million guilders in its financial year to January 31, 1997, down 58 percent from the 146.2 million one year earlier.
The 1995/96 figure included an extraordinary gain of 47.6 million guilders.

The figure which KBB now expects is at the upper end of a profit range given by the company in earlier statements. Last January, KBB said it expected the 1996/97 net profit to fall to between 55 and 60 million guilders.
KBB said the profits fall was mainly caused by disappointing results at its fashion chain M&S Mode where high discounts were necessary to reduce high inventories to a normal level.
A more cautious purchasing policy at M&S Mode and a better match between the unit's product range, shops, advertising and targeted customer base should improve results, KBB said.

It said its Bijenkorf department store had realised a substantial increase of operating results on four percent higher turnover. The Hema chain of department stores had posted clearly higher operating profits on sales which grew by more than five percent.
KBB's department stores posted 1996/97 turnover of 3.21 billion guilders, up from 3.05 billion in 1995/96, and operating profits rose to 113 million guilders from 85 million.

The company's specialty stores generated total sales of 2.72 billion guilders, compared with 2.82 billion in 1995/96. Operating profits plunged to 21 million guilders from 104 but KBB said this figure was distorted by the sale of the Bruna chain of bookstores at the end of 1995/96.
Interest charges rose by three million guilders to almost 24 million guilders, KBB said. The company will publish full 1996/97 figures and a dividend proposal on April 4.
